headline: This law makes Indian tribes eligible for AMBER Alert grants and helps link tribal alert systems with state systems.
what_it_does: It amends the PROTECT Act to renew the AMBER Alert grant program for fiscal year 2019. It adds linking tribal AMBER Alert systems with state systems as a new purpose for the grants. Tribes can now apply for these grants, and grant money can be used to connect state or regional alert plans with a tribe. The Justice Department must also report to Congress on the readiness, training, technology, and other obstacles tribes face in joining these systems.

who_it_affects.how: Tribes become eligible to receive AMBER Alert grants and may use them to connect with state or regional alert plans.

who_it_affects.group: State and regional AMBER Alert programs
who_it_affects.how: They can use grant funds to coordinate communication plans with neighboring tribes.

who_it_affects.group: Families of missing children on tribal lands
who_it_affects.how: Alerts may reach tribal communities more directly once tribal systems are linked to state systems.
It must study and report to Congress on the challenges tribes face in joining state alert systems.

when_it_takes_effect: Enacted April 13, 2018; the grant program reauthorization applies to fiscal year 2019.
